svg.title: Cloud Edge Collaboration Architecture
svg.desc: Three layers from top to bottom: cloud, edge, and devices. The cloud management plane covers edge node management (node batches, node groups), edge application management (application/model deployment, configs and secrets), edge device management (device creation, device twins), and data management (message endpoints, message routing), on top of a Kubernetes cluster and an operating system. The cloud delivers applications, configs, and models to the edge, while the edge uploads data and status back to the cloud. The edge layer runs applications and models, provides edge control (resource control, edge O&M, application/model deployment, application/model logs, device data collection, device protocol conversion, data channels, message routing), a container engine, an operating system, and x86, ARM, network, compute, and storage infrastructure; it stays autonomous on weak or offline networks. The device layer consists of multi-protocol terminals (Modbus), smart IoT devices, and the DMI standard device interface, connected to the edge through device access and data collection. Orange dashed lines indicate application/config delivery, blue solid lines indicate data/status upload, and gray solid lines indicate device access.
